video_title: Why Reinsurance Could Become DeFi’s Best Collateral | Ryan Connor & Ayyan Rahman
gist: Henri's tokenized reinsurance product (onyc/ENYC) delivers double-digit, low-duration yield uncorrelated to crypto or equities, and has become Solana DeFi's most utilized RWA collateral (96% utilization, ~2/3 of supply looped on Kamino at 7%+ lending rates). Guests Ryan Connor (Rockaway X) and Ayyan Rahman (Henri co-founder) argue reinsurance's structural risk-return profile, improving climate/AI forecasting, and a still-tiny ~$300M onchain penetration of an $800B TAM make it a durable, underexploited yield source and DeFi collateral primitive.

insights.claim: Reinsurance is insurance for insurance companies: primary insurers underwrite policies (e.g., Florida homeowner storm coverage) up to a threshold, then cede losses above that threshold to reinsurers in exchange for a premium.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Basic mechanism investors need to understand before evaluating any reinsurance-linked yield product.

insights.claim: Henri's ENYC (onyc) token is structured so that $1 deposited returns $1 of onyc, with 85 cents placed in a Bank of New York Mellon treasuries trust as underwriting collateral alongside the cedant's premium payments, and the resulting yield stream accrues to onyc holders.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Clarifies exactly where onyc yield originates and how collateral is custodied, useful for underwriting the token's credit risk.

insights.claim: Henri underwrites primarily property catastrophe reinsurance across peak perils (US hurricanes, Japan typhoons, earthquakes, wildfires) plus a diversified book of worldwide catastrophe exposures, rather than concentrating in one geography like many traditional reinsurers.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Global diversification (versus a specialist reinsurer's regional book) is a risk-management differentiator worth checking against future disclosures.

insights.claim: Traditional reinsurance/ILS exposure has historically been gated to pension funds and private equity firms writing large checks, with multi-year lockups and only annual liquidity windows, and disclosure limited to quarterly reports on roughly a one-month lag.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Explains the structural illiquidity/opacity gap that onchain reinsurance products like Henri are arbitraging.
insights.quote: I think the highest frequency data that you're going to get out of reinsurance funds in TRAFI is on a quarterly basis on a one-month lag

insights.claim: From 2006 onward, the S&P 500 annualized roughly 8% with about 15% volatility, while the Swiss Re Cat Bond Index annualized roughly 13% with about 2.8% volatility over the same period, giving reinsurance a markedly better risk-adjusted return profile than equities.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: A concrete long-run risk/return comparison an allocator can cite when sizing a reinsurance sleeve versus equities.
insights.quote: Reinsurance is annualizing I believe 13% keer uh the Swiss Recat Bond Index with 2.8% involved over the same period.

insights.claim: Reinsurance functions as portfolio ballast for bond managers because it offers high yield with low duration and low correlation to the economic cycle, unlike stretching for yield into equity-like credit risk that becomes correlated to defaults and mark-to-market swings.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Frames reinsurance as a distinct diversifier bond managers can add without taking on correlated credit/equity risk.

insights.claim: Unlike private credit, where a default impairs an issuer's access to credit for the next four to five years, a major catastrophe loss event in property-cat reinsurance is typically followed by rates increasing significantly, making it the best time to write new reinsurance business.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Counterintuitive: loss events in reinsurance improve forward return prospects, unlike credit markets where defaults are persistently damaging — implies reinsurers should have dry powder to deploy post-event.

insights.claim: Roughly two-thirds of total onyc supply is deposited on Kamino (Solana lending market), making Henri's onyc the largest RWA market by deposits on that platform.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Concentration of a young RWA's float into one lending venue is a real usage signal but also a venue-concentration risk to monitor.

insights.claim: Lenders supplying USDC against onyc collateral on Kamino earn over 7%, versus the roughly 3-4% typical for DeFi lending, while being protected by an LTV structure that provides about a 28% first-loss buffer before their principal is at risk.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: A specific risk-adjusted yield number lenders can compare against other DeFi lending markets before allocating.
insights.quote: you're being able to earn almost over 7% on USDC which is pretty unheard of especially when it comes to lending traditionally in DeFi markets

insights.claim: On DeFiLlama's RWA page, Henri's onyc shows roughly 96% utilization (DeFi TVL used versus total TVL), the highest of any RWA category, in contrast to other hyped RWAs like private credit, which the host notes is held by around 100 addresses and rarely moved or used as collateral.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Utilization, not just TVL, is the metric to watch for which RWAs are actually functioning as productive DeFi collateral versus parked assets.
insights.quote: reinsurance TVL specifically Henry is at 96% utilization in D5

insights.claim: The Exponent protocol splits tokenized onyc into principal and yield components, letting participants speculate purely on the yield stream or separate exposure into senior and junior (credit-tranched) tokens for different risk appetites.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Credit tranching of an RWA yield stream onchain is a new primitive — watch Exponent volumes as a proxy for institutional-grade DeFi credit product adoption.

insights.claim: The real innovation of tokenizing real-world assets is not digitization/distribution alone but restructuring the asset itself to be usable as productive collateral across DeFi — without that, tokenization just adds liquidity options without adding utility.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: A filter for evaluating any RWA project: ask whether the underlying asset's terms were re-engineered for composability, not just wrapped in a token.
insights.quote: I think what a lot of people do wrong is that they assume that tokenization itself is the innovation

insights.claim: Investors are already using onyc as collateral to borrow and redeploy capital into other speculative crypto opportunities, effectively using the uncorrelated yield asset to increase capital efficiency during a bull market.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Signals onyc is being adopted as a base-layer collateral asset analogous to stablecoins, which could compound demand independent of yield-seeking alone.

insights.claim: Henri reserves 50% of total annual premiums as a buffer specifically because reinsurance risk is seasonal (e.g., concentrated in hurricane season), rather than releasing all premium income upfront, so that reserve layer absorbs losses before NAV/collateral is touched.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Explains the loss-absorption waterfall (earned premium -> reserved premium -> NAV/collateral) investors should model before sizing leverage.
insights.quote: we reserve across the entire year 50% of total premiums

insights.claim: Per Ali Labs' risk analysis, Henri's worst-case NAV drawdown scenario is modeled at roughly 20%, characterized as a one-in-100-year event.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Gives loopers/lenders a concrete tail-risk figure to stress-test their leverage and LTV assumptions against.
insights.quote: the worst case scenario that we've done analysis for is like a 20% nav draw down scenario, which is like a one in 100year event

insights.claim: In a prior severe Florida hurricane (around 2017-2019), at least one ILS fund lost its entire annual yield — investors received 0% instead of an expected ~11% — illustrating the realistic downside case for reinsurance exposure rather than a principal wipeout.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Sets investor expectations: the typical tail outcome in this asset class is a lost year of yield, not necessarily large principal loss.
insights.quote: there was like one ILS fund that lost all their yield for the year

insights.claim: Because onyc's NAV is set by an offchain oracle rather than real-time market pricing, a catastrophe event does not trigger instant liquidations the way a live-priced asset would; Henri's underwriting team aims to update NAV onchain within about 24 hours of an event to keep the oracle price close to true value.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: The lag between real-world loss events and onchain NAV marks is a structural risk for leveraged loopers — a fast-moving event could leave collateral mispriced for up to a day.

insights.claim: Kamino and Ali Labs calibrate onyc's LTV and maximum leverage parameters against real historical catastrophe data (backtesting how past events would have impacted NAV) rather than generic risk assumptions, and Ali Labs publishes a dashboard letting users simulate liquidation thresholds at different leverage levels.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Actionable due-diligence step: loopers can use the Ali Labs dashboard to test their specific leverage against historical catastrophe scenarios before sizing a position.

insights.claim: NOAA data on landfall hurricanes shows a secular decline in frequency over the last three decades, and California wildfire frequency has been roughly constant — the apparent rise in catastrophe losses is driven mainly by increased building in fire- and storm-prone areas, not by more frequent events.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Challenges the popular narrative that climate change is straightforwardly increasing catastrophe frequency — reinsurance investors who get comfortable with this data can underwrite tail risk more confidently than the general public assumes.
insights.quote: if you look at the data from Noah and you look at landfall hurricanes, you will see that they are in secular decline over the last three decades

insights.claim: As of recording (peak 2025 Atlantic hurricane season), the ACE (Accumulated Cyclone Energy) index measuring storm intensity is at its lowest level in the 60-year historical dataset, implying an unusually low realized probability of a major landfall event this season so far.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: A live, checkable data point (ACE index) that reinsurance-exposed investors can monitor in real time as a leading indicator for Henri's Q3/Q4 NAV risk.
insights.quote: It's the lowest that it's been in the 60 years of the data set and like right now is peak hurricane season.

insights.claim: AI weather models (referenced by the guests as a Google storm-prediction service) have become more accurate than some national weather administrations at forecasting hurricane paths and formation, enabling reinsurance participants to better hedge or take out puts on their book ahead of storms.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Improving AI forecast accuracy is a structural tailwind for reinsurer loss ratios and a potential edge source for actively-hedged books.

insights.claim: Hurricane forecasting has improved so much that today's 7-day forecast is roughly as accurate as a 1-day forecast was 20 years ago, representing a secular tailwind that should reduce loss volatility for the reinsurance asset class over time.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Improving forecast accuracy is a structural driver that could compress reinsurance loss volatility and support further yield-for-risk improvement over multi-year holding periods.
insights.quote: the 7-day forecasts today are as accurate as like the one-day forecast like 20 years ago

insights.claim: As AI and technology reduce reinsurance's reliance on brokers and middlemen and lower the industry's expense ratio, the likely effect is more capital entering the space (lower access barriers) rather than compressed yields for end investors.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Implies AUM growth in reinsurance-linked products (including onyc) could accelerate as distribution costs fall, without necessarily eroding the yield investors capture.

themes.theme: TAM, Growth Trajectory & Broader RWA Thesis

insights.claim: Total global reinsurance market is roughly $800 billion, TradFi ILS mutual funds/hedge fund exposure is about $6-8 billion, and onchain reinsurance exposure is effectively only Henri at roughly $300 million — implying the onchain segment has penetrated well under 1% of the addressable TAM.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: Quantifies enormous headroom for onchain reinsurance issuance growth if Henri (or competitors) can scale distribution.
insights.quote: Onchain it's basically only Henry and it's 300 million and it's a fundamentally better product.

insights.claim: Tokenized Strategies preferred equity ('stretch') reached an outlier 3-5% penetration of its offchain issuance as tokenized supply, versus typical RWAs that penetrate only a few basis points of their offchain TAM — a useful high-water-mark comparison for how far onchain reinsurance could scale.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Sets a precedent ceiling (3-5%) for how much of an offchain asset class can realistically migrate onchain, useful for sizing Henri's long-run TAM capture.

insights.claim: Ryan Connor predicts Henri will reach roughly $10 billion in AUM within about three years, driven by differentiated (not commoditized) yield exposure that TradFi rails can't easily replicate.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: A specific, falsifiable AUM target investors can track as a benchmark for whether onchain reinsurance is scaling as bullishly as its proponents claim.
insights.quote: three years from now, we'll do this podcast again. uh Henry is going to have 10 billion in AUM

insights.claim: Henri chose to launch on Solana over Ethereum because Solana had far fewer competing RWA issuers at the time and its DeFi infrastructure (Kamino's multiply product, Loopscale's vault infrastructure) already supported automated looping from day one, whereas EVM ecosystems only recently began building comparable auto-loop infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Explains a concrete infra/competition-driven reason for chain selection — relevant for evaluating whether new RWA issuers will keep favoring Solana or shift to EVM as its looping infra matures.

insights.claim: Henri's current growth bottleneck is not asset-side demand but finding new lending venues/ecosystems, since its Kamino markets already run at roughly 90-95% utilization most of the time — implying more onchain distribution partners, not more supply, unlocks the next leg of growth.
insights.speaker: Ayyan Rahman
insights.so_what: Watch for new lending-market integrations (beyond Kamino/Solana) as the key catalyst for onyc's next growth phase rather than watching NAV/issuance alone.

insights.claim: Onchain RWA issuance only makes sense for assets offering differentiated exposure that's hard to access in TradFi (like reinsurance); tokenizing assets with already-ample TradFi access, such as Treasuries, adds little value since the existing rails are 'good enough' and onchain markets are already saturated with tokenized Treasury yield.
insights.speaker: Ryan Connor
insights.so_what: A screening heuristic for evaluating future RWA launches: prioritize issuers bringing genuinely new/scarce exposure onchain over those repackaging commoditized TradFi yield.
insights.quote: I just don't think it's the case that people holding and trading these assets really really care where they exist.
